title: Interface Specification: the power-path switch and contactor-feedback interface

standards_mappings.rationale: Backs SWE.2 with a real interface specification: providing and consuming module, the real C signature transcribed from the header at 308028fb, per-parameter direction, unit, meaning and valid range with the mechanism that enforces it, a return contract whose values are the enumerators the source defines, validity signalling read off the real error paths, timing where the source imposes one, concurrency, and a required not_specified_by_source list. Three elements: the periodic control function, the command entry point and the feedback read. The status stays partially_mapped: the whole family remains a reconstruction of an existing implementation rather than the product of an architectural design activity, and Component Design remains absent.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('backs '): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. providing_module.name: SPS driver, the power-path switch and port-expander feedback
providing_module.role: Drives the high-side switches that carry current in the contactor bank, records the commanded state, and reads each channel's feedback either as a port-expander pin level or as a measured contactor current. It is the layer between the contactor driver's contactor abstraction and the physical switching devices.

consuming_modules.name: Contactor driver
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: CONT_OpenContactor calls SPS_RequestContactorState at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L176; the contactor design record FB2-SW-DSN-000006 names SPS_RequestContactorState, SPS_GetChannelPexFeedback and SPS_GetChannelCurrentFeedback as the contactor driver's outbound calls. CONT_GetContactorState at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L246 is the consumer-side entry point that leads here.

values.(no return value): The function returns nothing; its whole effect is on the switch state and the command buffer.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A void control entry point gives the caller no way to learn whether the cycle ran to completion.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L87 declares void; src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L486 is the definition.

validity_signalling.mechanism: No return value. The re-entrance guard exits silently.
validity_signalling.evidence: The header states the function exits without effect on re-entrance at src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L84-L85, so a caller that double-calls cannot tell the second call did nothing.

timing.evidence: The header states the function must be called time-triggered every 10 ms at src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L84.

concurrency.evidence: Called from the 10 ms cyclic task; the header documents both the period and the re-entrance exit at src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L84-L85. The SPI transfer the cycle performs takes the SPI lock specified in FB2-SW-IFS-000008 at src/app/driver/spi/spi.c L513.
concurrency.protection_mechanism: re-entrance flag tested before any state change

error_paths.observed_behaviour: The function returns having changed nothing.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L84-L85 states the exit without effect.

error_paths.condition: either half of the daisy-chain SPI transmit fails
error_paths.observed_behaviour: SPS_Transmit returns STD_NOT_OK and the channel is not treated as commanded.
error_paths.evidence: The two SPI results are combined and STD_NOT_OK returned unless both are STD_OK at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L456-L460; the result is tested at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L517 and again per channel at L531, L542, L553, L565, L577 and L589.

not_specified_by_source: The source does not state what a caller should do when a cycle is skipped by re-entrance; it states only that it exits.
No counter of skipped or failed cycles is exposed, so a persistent SPI failure is not observable through this interface.
The header attributes the function to the CONT driver's state machine at src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L82, which does not name the module that owns it.

parameters.name: channelIndex
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT(channelIndex < SPS_NR_OF_AVAILABLE_SPS_CHANNELS) at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L477 inside the static SPS_RequestChannelState this function delegates to, and again at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L642. SPS_NR_OF_AVAILABLE_SPS_CHANNELS is SPS_NR_CONTACTOR_PER_IC * SPS_NR_OF_IC at src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h L102 and SPS_NR_CONTACTOR_PER_IC is 4u at src/app/driver/config/sps_cfg.h L82.

parameters.name: channelFunction
parameters.meaning: The state to command onto the channel.
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT((channelFunction == SPS_CHANNEL_OFF) || (channelFunction == SPS_CHANNEL_ON)) at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L478.

values.(no return value): Nothing is returned; the request is recorded and acted on by the next SPS_Ctrl cycle.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A request naming a channel affiliated to general IO rather than to a contactor is not accepted, and the caller cannot tell.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L97 declares void; src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L607 is the definition.

validity_signalling.mechanism: No return value. A rejected request is discarded silently.
validity_signalling.evidence: src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L612 asserts the channel's affiliation is SPS_AFF_CONTACTOR, so a caller naming a general-IO channel traps rather than receiving an error, and there is no return value with which to report a refusal.

timing.evidence: Not periodic. The request is recorded and applied by the 10 ms cycle on IFSE-000901, so the effect appears at the next cycle boundary; the interface does not state that latency.

concurrency.evidence: Called by the contactor driver from a task. The static it delegates to writes the command buffer under the SPS task critical section at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L466-L474; the entry point itself takes no lock.

error_paths.condition: channel is not a contactor channel
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The affiliation assertion fires; the request is not applied.

error_paths.condition: channelFunction is neither OFF nor ON
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The precondition assertion fires before the request is recorded.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state how long a recorded request may wait before SPS_Ctrl applies it.
It does not return the previously commanded state, so a caller cannot read back what it last asked for.
It does not state what happens to a request whose switch feedback disagrees with it; feedback is read through a separate entry point.

elements.declaration: extern CONT_ELECTRICAL_STATE_TYPE_e SPS_GetChannelPexFeedback(const SPS_CHANNEL_INDEX channelIndex, bool normallyOpen);

parameters.name: channelIndex
parameters.meaning: Which SPS channel to read the feedback of.

parameters.name: normallyOpen
parameters.unit: contact kind (true for normally open feedback)
parameters.meaning: Whether the feedback pin is a normally-open or normally-closed contact, which inverts the level that means closed.
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT((normallyOpen == true) || (normallyOpen == false)) at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L643.

values.CONT_SWITCH_ON: The pin level is interpreted as closed: high for a normally-open contact, low for a normally-closed contact.
values.CONT_SWITCH_OFF: The pin level is the opposite of closed.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: The return carries only the two electrical states, so a genuinely open circuit, a shorted feedback line and an open contactor are all reported as CONT_SWITCH_OFF.
return_contract.evidence: The two-state assignment is at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L648-L659 reading the pin at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L646; the enumerators are CONT_ELECTRICAL_STATE_TYPE_e from the contactor boundary FB2-SW-IFS-000003.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Return value only. There is no error channel distinct from the two states.
validity_signalling.evidence: src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L661 returns the state directly; PEX_GetPin at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L646 has no failure result that this function inspects, and the header documents the return only as the state of the channel at src/app/driver/sps/sps.h L126.

timing.evidence: A synchronous read of one pin through the port expander; the source states no period for the read itself and no settling interval between a command and a readable feedback level.

concurrency.evidence: Called by the contactor driver's feedback task; the function reads a configuration table entry and one port-expander pin with no lock. The port expander is anchored at src/app/driver/config/pex_cfg.h L73-L97.

error_paths.condition: channelIndex at or above the channel count

error_paths.observed_behaviour: Not detected. The value read is used as if it were a valid level.
error_paths.evidence: PEX_GetPin is assigned to pinState at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L646 with no check between that assignment and the comparisons at L651 and L656.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state the debounce or settling time between commanding a contactor and reading its feedback pin, which is what makes a closure claim meaningful.
It does not return a timestamp or age, so a caller cannot distinguish a fresh reading from a stale one.
It does not distinguish a feedback-line fault from a genuinely open contactor, because both produce CONT_SWITCH_OFF.

interface_level_gaps.gap: A contactor feedback read returns a two-state electrical value with no fault state, no freshness and no settling time, so the interface cannot distinguish a closed contactor from a broken feedback line.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The contactor driver, which is the mechanism that raises a contactor-feedback diagnosis, receives the same value for both, so the second indication of a contactor's state is not independent of the feedback wiring.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: SPS_GetChannelPexFeedback returns only CONT_SWITCH_ON or CONT_SWITCH_OFF from src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L648-L661 and the pin read at L646 is not checked.

interface_level_gaps.gap: Commanding a switch and reading its feedback are two separate entry points with no shared transaction and no timeout between them.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A caller can request a state, observe no confirmation, and has no interface-level way to decide whether the request is in flight, has been dropped, or has been applied with the feedback lagging.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: SPS_RequestContactorState at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L607 records a request and returns void; SPS_GetChannelPexFeedback at src/app/driver/sps/sps.c L641 reads a pin; neither states a settling interval and no transaction identifier exists between them.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Three elements over the power-path switch boundary, read from sps.h, sps_types.h and sps.c at 308028fb. The boundary matters because the contactor driver reads contactor feedback through it, and that feedback is one of the two independent indications a contactor-closure claim rests on. No source-registry anchor exists for sps.c at this commit; the nearest real anchors are the SPI boundary the cycle depends on and the contactor boundary it serves, and the record says so rather than citing an anchor that does not exist.
